verdict: Buildable and demoable by 14:30, and the deployment story is genuinely bulletproof (static Vite, no backend, every one of the 14 pinned npm versions exists, peer ranges all satisfied: plugin-react 6.1.2 wants vite ^8, postprocessing 6.39.5 wants three >=0.168 <0.187, fiber 9.8.2 wants react >=19 <19.4, drei 10.7.9 wants fiber ^9; HF mirror vancevo/online-retail-ii resolves, 7,156,732 bytes, PAR1, 1,067,371 rows, both sheets, Dec 2009 to Dec 2011). But I replicated prep.py on the real parquet and several load-bearing claims are wrong as written. (1) The demo script's hero fact is false: the hottest Nov 2011 SKU is 23084 RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT at 487 pick lines; 85123A WHITE HANGING HEART is 6th at 250, not "1,2xx"; the scripted affinity pair 85123A+85099B co-occurs in only 47 orders while the true top pairs are 22086+22910 PAPER CHAIN KITs (198) and 22577+22578 WOODEN HEART/STAR (189). Saying a number on stage that the screen contradicts reads as fabrication. (2) "Exact Held-Karp" is the exception, not the rule: 316 of 2,359 orders (13.4%) have >12 top-100 lines and they carry 43.3% of all pick lines (mean 7.2 lines/order, median 5, p90 15, max 76), so roughly half of the walking is routed heuristically. (3) The SA budget is off by two orders of magnitude: the hottest SKU is in 20.6% of orders, median SKU in 6.5%; a random swap on the 600-order subsample touches 75 orders (max 162) and costs ~17 ms to re-route with DP cap 12, so the "8 s live" run gets ~470 moves and the "60 s offline" run ~3,500, far too few for SA over a 112-slot permutation; the live objective curve will be nearly flat and the "AI opponent" segment risks showing ~0% over baseline. (4) Several engineering specs are self-contradicting: the drift test compares a results.md that embeds commit hash and timestamp, so it always fails; vitest ^3 bundles its own vite 7 (deps.vite ^5||^6||^7) under a vite 8 app, vitest 4.1+/5 is required; integration at 03:30-05:00 is labelled "humans + one agent" while humans sleep 01:30-07:30; the Kaggle anonymous fallback URL returns 404. None of this is fatal, all of it is fixable in the first two hours, and the fixed version is an 8+. As written, the headline claims would be either false or embarrassingly weak on stage.
weaknesses: Demo script data facts are wrong: hottest Nov 2011 SKU is 23084 RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT (487 pick lines), then 22086 PAPER CHAIN KIT 50'S CHRISTMAS (390), 23355 HOT WATER BOTTLE KEEP CALM (288), 22910 (276), 23344 (266), 85123A (250, 6th), 85099B (247); the 100th SKU has 119 picks. The scripted tooltip '85123A · 1,2xx picks' is ~5x off and the scripted affinity pair (85123A+85099B, 47 co-orders) is not an affinity pair.

Exact-routing claim is misleading: with DP cap 12, 13.4% of orders (316/2,359) and 43.3% of pick lines are routed by NN+2-opt; raising the cap to 14 still leaves 10.4% of orders / 37.8% of lines (DP at n=14 costs 6.7 ms/order measured in Node, n=16 ~35 ms, so the cap cannot go much higher). The Q&A card 'why DP is exact' must become 'exact for orders <=12 stops, which is X% of orders and Y% of distance'.

SA throughput math is broken: measured Held-Karp costs 0.016 ms (n=6), 0.26 ms (n=10), 1.35 ms (n=12); a swap touches mean 75 orders of the 600-order subsample (hottest SKU in 20.6% of orders, median SKU 6.5%, min 5.0%), ~17 ms per move, p90 22 ms => ~470 moves in 8 s, ~3,500 in 60 s. SA needs 10^5+ moves to do anything over a 112-slot permutation. Also allocating a fresh 196 KB Float32Array per DP call will GC-thrash inside the worker loop.

Expected SA gain over the ABC baseline is small and may be ~0 on held-out: 14.8% of orders are single-line (zero affinity benefit), true co-pick pairs are mostly StockCode-adjacent product families (22577/22578/22579, 23343/23344, 22726/22727) with similar pick counts, which the frequency-sorted baseline already places in adjacent slots. The 'AI opponent beats baseline by Y%' segment may read 1-3% in-sample and ~0% held-out; the narrative must be prepared for that.

A human player beating the fast-movers baseline live is improbable (baseline is near-optimal for short orders). The ghost race is against Original (StockCode order), which is fine, but the KPI card will show Player < Baseline unless the rehearsed hash layout starts from the SA/baseline layout.

Drift test as specified always fails: eval/results.md embeds commit hash and generated_at, so a fresh run never byte-matches. Must compare only the numeric table block (or write the header to a separate file).

vitest ^3 is wrong for Vite 8: vitest 3.2.7 depends on vite ^5||^6||^7 (nested second vite, config incompatibilities with rolldown-era options); vitest 4.1.x and 5.0.5 accept vite ^8. Stack also omits @tailwindcss/vite (4.3.3, peer vite ^8 OK) which Tailwind 4 needs under Vite.

Timeline contradiction: 'Integration + QA (humans + one agent) 03:30-05:00' while 'humans sleep 01:30-07:30'. Overnight the hourly-commit cadence depends on agents that stall on the first permission prompt, merge conflict or failing build; a 6-hour commit gap and an un-merged branch pile at 07:30 is the realistic outcome unless one human stays on a 2-hour watch rotation.

Explainability budget is unrealistic: sim (graph, DP, NN/2-opt/Or-opt, S-shape, return, SA with delta eval), worker protocol, zustand store, 10+ R3F components, post-FX tiering, 2D SVG map, eval script, prep.py, tests is ~5-7k LOC; 07:30-09:30 is 2 h for humans who did not write it. Scope must be cut, not just documented.

HF mirror provenance is thin: README has no licence, no source link, 17 downloads, created 2026-05-11; every column is a string dtype (Quantity, Price, InvoiceDate all need casting, which does work cleanly with 0 nulls). A judge asking 'how do you know this mirror is faithful?' has no answer unless you also hash it against the UCI zip (which resolves, HTTP 200).
Kaggle anonymous fallback URL (kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/mashlyn/online-retail-ii-uci) returns 404; only the UCI zip (43.5 MB) is a working fallback.

drei DragControls (confirmed in 10.7.9: wraps children in a THREE.Group, @use-gesture based) cannot drag one instance of an InstancedMesh; 3D drag needs a proxy mesh spawned on pointerdown with event.instanceId. The plan already makes click-to-swap primary, but Agent C's 1.5 h estimate for 'DragControls snapping in 3D' is for a feature that needs a different design.

Windows MAX_PATH: this machine's workspace path is ~175 chars and already broke Python opening a file in the scratchpad (ENOENT at ~280 chars). node_modules/@rolldown/binding-win32-x64-msvc/*.node plus vite cache will hit 260 chars under that path; the repo must be cloned at a short path (e.g. C:\hack\reslot).

Dark #0b1020 scene on a venue projector washes out; no light/projector theme is planned. 5-minute script has 7 segments and ~20 clicks including an 8 s live optimiser wait; hackathon demos run 20-30% over.

Non-product filter regex ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ also drops real products like DCGSSGIRL and DCGS* codes (only 278 lines in Nov, of which POST 164, DOT 47, M 41, C2 23, BANK CHARGES 2), harmless for ranking but should be stated as 'alphanumeric-only codes dropped', not 'non-product codes'.
fixes: Replace every data fact in the demo script with values printed by prep.py: hottest box = 23084 RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT (487), affinity demo pair = 22086 PAPER CHAIN KIT 50'S CHRISTMAS + 22910 PAPER CHAIN KIT VINTAGE CHRISTMAS (198 co-orders) or 22577+22578 WOODEN HEART/STAR CHRISTMAS SCANDINAVIAN (189). Add a rule: nothing is spoken that is not read off the Data panel.

Fix SA cost: run the annealing loop on a surrogate objective that is O(lines) per order (S-shape or return-policy distance, which the plan already implements), with the SKU->orders index and a 300-order subsample, then score the result with the exact simulate at the end and on milestones. That yields ~50k-100k moves in 8 s. Pre-allocate one dp Float32Array per worker for the DP. Ship a 10-minute offline SA result as layouts/sa_seed42.json and label the live 8 s run as 'continue from shipped solution', never as the full optimisation.

Reframe routing honesty: Evidence panel shows 'exact DP (<=12 stops): N orders, X% of distance; heuristic NN+2-opt: M orders, Y% of distance' with the measured numbers (expect ~87% of orders, ~55% of lines exact). Change the Q&A card to 'exact for <=12 stops, heuristic above, same policy both layouts'. Keep cap 12 (measured 1.35 ms at n=12, 6.7 ms at n=14, ~35 ms at n=16).

Pre-build the player's rehearsed layout from the shipped SA layout plus 2-3 manual swaps and keep its hash in the clipboard; plan the KPI card narrative for Player ~ SA > Baseline >> Original. Add a 'Start from baseline' button so a live player edit begins from a competitive layout.

Drift test: eval writes eval/results.md (numbers only, deterministic) and eval/results.meta.json (hash, timestamp); the vitest test compares only results.md. Pin vitest ^4.1 (or 5.0.5) and add @tailwindcss/vite@4.3.3 to the stack.

Fix the schedule: either one human stays awake 01:30-04:00 and another 04:00-07:30 as merge/permission watch, or move integration to 07:30-09:00 and accept a documented commit gap (DEV_LOG entry 'team sleeping 01:30-07:30'). Run agents with pre-approved permissions for npm/git/vite in the repo so they do not stall.

Cut scope to protect explainability: drop return-policy routing, Or-opt, configurable layout, post-FX (Bloom/SMAA) and the 3D DragControls; keep DP+NN/2-opt, S-shape (needed as the SA surrogate), click-to-swap in 3D and 2D, ghost race, heat racks, box-fly. Target <=3k LOC with a one-paragraph header per file; assign each file to a named human by 07:30.

Provenance: tonight also download the UCI zip (archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/502/online+retail+ii.zip, HTTP 200) once, record its SHA-256 and the parquet's SHA-256 in data/README.md, and have prep.py assert row count 1,067,371 and the Nov 2011 counts (84,711 raw lines, 3,462 invoices, 441 C-invoices, 1,365 exact duplicates, 2,751 invoices after cleaning, top-100 coverage 21.2%, 2,359 orders, split 1,130/1,229). Delete the Kaggle fallback from the docs.
Clone the repo at C:\hack\reslot (short path) before npm install; enable Windows long paths as belt-and-braces (git config core.longpaths true).

Add a 'Projector' theme toggle (light floor, dark racks, high-contrast path) and cut the live demo to 5 segments: intro flight + heat racks + data panel (0:45), replay with counters (0:45), baseline + player swap + ghost race (1:30), optimiser result applied from shipped JSON with a 5 s live continuation (0:45), evidence table + limitations (0:45), team (0:15). Move routing ablation and share-link to Q&A cards.

Consider top-150 SKUs in 8x2x10=160 slots if Agent A finishes early: coverage rises from 21.2% to 27.9% (top-200: 33.6%) at little cost; whole-month exact scoring stays well under 1 s (estimated ~260 ms at cap 12 for top-100).
steal_worthy: Pure-static deployment with triple hosting (Vercel + Cloudflare Pages + local vite preview) and zero runtime network calls: no cold start, no keys, no rate limits; the single best demo-safety pattern among the 12 problems.

One headless, deterministic simulate(layout, orders, policy) shared by the UI, the Web Worker and an npm run eval script, with a drift test tying README numbers to the app (once the hash/timestamp bug is fixed).

In-app provenance: Data panel showing meta counts at every cleaning stage verbatim from the prep script, clickable boxes showing StockCode + pick count, and a time-based opt/held-out split shown on screen.
Ghost-vs-solid replay race on identical orders with live diverging counters: 'measured, not claimed' made visible.
InstancedMesh heat racks + floor-tile visit heat (2-3 draw calls) and a 2 s FPS probe that picks a quality tier, with a 2D SVG slot map as a complete fallback and phone view.
Held-Karp exact routing for small orders with a flagged heuristic above a cap, measured timings (1.35 ms at n=12) and a per-order 'exact vs heuristic' count in the evidence panel.
